subject.title: fix(gateway): avoid stale wake delays after node re-pairing

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this branch-wide pairing-generation authority model across node runtime, persisted pairing state, and APNs delivery, or should the fix be narrowed to the removal and wake-state paths that originally regressed?
rationale: The PR changes authorization and ownership semantics across gateway transports and persistent state; code review alone cannot safely choose the intended long-term boundary.

options.title: Approve the generation model after owner review
options.body: Keep the cross-path fence if the gateway owner confirms it is the canonical authority boundary and the current-head CodeQL result is clean.

options.title: Narrow the repair
options.body: Retain only the shared removal cleanup and generation-scoped wake/pending-work changes if the broader session and transport redesign is not intended.

recommendation.title: Approve the generation model after owner review
recommendation.body: Keep the cross-path fence if the gateway owner confirms it is the canonical authority boundary and the current-head CodeQL result is clean.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the proposed end-to-end design and can clarify the intended invariants while a gateway-area reviewer decides whether to adopt them.
